pr_title: Fallback to config entry ID as unique ID when serialno is not available for APCUPSD
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

For some dumb APC UPSes the daemon might not report `SERIALNO`, in which case we should fall back to use config entry ID as the unique ID per [dev docs](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/entity_registry_index?_highlight=unique#unique-id-of-last-resort).

This PR adds such handling such that APC UPS entities should always have an unique ID to be registered. Tests are also updated to reflect this change.

> The major concern is whether an APC UPS might "lose" (if previously available) or "gain" (if previously unavailable) a serial number, maybe via firmware upgrade/downgrade.

I don't think that's possible, judging from the APC UPS daemon C code:

```c
   if (ups->UPS_Cap[CI_SERNO])
      s_write(ups, "SERIALNO : %s\n", ups->serial);
```

It basically just checks if the UPS is capable of providing a serial number and then writes it to the report. Now the firmware on the UPSes could be really weird that it stops providing a serial number, but my APC UPSes basically never do that. 

> You can take a look at https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/129133
> It's not exactly the same - but it might give you inspiration...

Thanks for the pointer, so the logic there is basically trying to migrate an existing old unique ID to a new format, such that it basically iterates the entity registries and update the unique ID instead. 

Here, since the old entities basically didn't have unique IDs, they are probably not part of the registry? I'm a bit lost on how to properly migrate this case.

Yes, `SERIALNO` being reported as `Blank` is treated the same as no `SERIALNO` being reported at all: it means that we do not have a unique ID for the device, and that is causing issue for HA to create entities.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/130852 should fix this by falling back to use the config ID as the unique ID, which should fix this issue (I think)

review_comments: I think you can set this in the constructor to an attribute itself so it doesn't have to evaluate for every entity again.

I don't think so. Judging from the source code:

```c
   if (ups->UPS_Cap[CI_SERNO])
      s_write(ups, "SERIALNO : %s\n", ups->serial);
```

(where `UPS_Cap` is the static capability array of the UPS).

~Updated here. PTAL.~

Actually, here we need to wait for the first refresh in order for `self.data` to be populated, right? such that we can't compute this in the constructor. We can:

(1) do an initial refresh in the constructor, but I think we generally rely on `await coordinator.async_config_entry_first_refresh()` in the `async_setup_entry`?
(2) cache the result in an attribute.

Since this is fairly fast and is only executed once (although for every entity) during setup, it's probably not worth it to implement either (1) or (2)?

> do an initial refresh in the constructor, but I think we generally rely on await coordinator.async_config_entry_first_refresh() in the async_setup_entry?

Yes, what does the code currently do?

> Yes, what does the code currently do?

In `async_setup_entry`, we construct the coordinator -> call `coordinator.async_config_entry_first_refresh()` which would populate the `coordinator.data` field -> later when the entities are created they will call this method here that reads data from `data` field.

So it's not really possible to store this in the constructor (the `data` field isn't populated yet when constructed).
